title: How Many Turns? Rotational Motion Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A mixer whirs up to speed. A potter's wheel spins faster with each kick. A giant wheel slows to a stop. When Aarav switches on his ceiling fan, it speeds up for a few seconds. How many turns does it make before it reaches full speed, without counting? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn angular acceleration and the equations of rotational motion with a steady angular acceleration.

On a live motion notebook a fan seen from below speeds up at 4 rad/s squared while the readout tracks t, omega, alpha, theta and the number of turns, and the omega-t graph climbs in a straight line with the angle turned shaded as the area under it. A slow-mo replay freezes at 2 s to show the blade tip's speed r omega and its tangential acceleration r alpha, and we switch the fan off to see alpha point the other way. We build the three equations step by step from the linear ones, see link by link why the tip gains speed fastest, compare a bike and a fan side by side, and count the fan's turns in a worked example. Then the exam trap (theta is in radians, divide by 2 pi for turns), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
